---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/asciimoo/hister
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/asciimoo/hister pinned by digest (the registry has no tag for this release)
  port: 4433
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: none, SQLite on the same volume as the index (see the quirk, this is deliberate)
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: hister
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ UNDERSTAND WHAT THIS INSTANCE WILL HOLD BEFORE YOU DEPLOY IT, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST SENSITIVE THING IN THIS LIBRARY. Hister is a personal search engine over the pages its owner VISITS. A browser extension pushes every page to it and Hister keeps the URL, the title, the extracted text AND, by default, a gzipped copy of the FULL HTML of every page, on disk, for previews (configuration.md:794-804). That means the search index, the cached page bodies and the visit history of somebody's actual browsing, including whatever was on the screen behind a login. Upstream says it plainly in their own server-setup guide: Hister transmits your entire browsing history, with page contents, to and from the server. Treat this deploy accordingly."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, AND WITH THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS EVERY ANONYMOUS REQUEST IS ALREADY TREATED AS AUTHENTICATED. This is not an inference, it is server/server.go:296-302: when neither app.user_handling nor app.access_token is set, the request context is created with Authenticated = true, and server.go:200-212 attaches no auth middleware to any route at all. There is no signup form, no install wizard and no default password, so there is nothing for a first visitor to claim, because a first visitor already has everything. THE RECIPE THEREFORE SETS HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN AT DEPLOY TIME, before the hostname is ever reachable, which is the safe-by-construction case. Do not deploy this app without it, and do not plan to add it afterwards."
  - "IS REGISTRATION OPEN AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT: THERE IS NO SELF-REGISTRATION AT ALL, WITH ONE EXCEPTION THAT MATTERS. In the default single-user mode there are no accounts. With app.user_handling enabled there are, but they can only be created by running hister create-user on the server host, because the user commands operate on the database directly rather than over the API, so no web request can ever create one. ⚠️ THE EXCEPTION: if you configure server.oauth, a first sign-in through GitHub, Google or OIDC AUTOMATICALLY CREATES a local account (user-handling.md:34). That turns registration into open registration to every user of that provider. Do not configure OAuth on a personal instance unless the user has asked for it and understands that."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ONCE THE ACCESS TOKEN IS SET: six endpoints, none of which serves indexed content. Verified by reading the whole routing table in server/api.go, where exactly six entries carry NoAuth true: GET /api/config (server name, hotkeys, auth mode, CSRF token, and NOT the access token itself), GET /api/extractors, POST /api/login, POST /api/token-login, GET /api/oauth and GET /api/oauth/callback. Everything that can read content, meaning GET /search, /api/document, /api/preview, /api/file, /api/facets, /api/stats, /api/versions and POST /mcp, is refused with 403 by withTokenAuth (server.go:336-357). GET /api/history is refused even in public mode."
  - "⛔ LEAVE app.public AT FALSE. It is the single switch that undoes the paragraph above. With app.public true, every endpoint marked Public in the routing table becomes anonymous: search, document reads, CACHED PAGE PREVIEWS, local FILE serving, facets, stats and the MCP search tool. Upstream's own warning is that only content intended for public access should be indexed on such an instance. Public mode is a real feature for a deliberately shared index, and it is the wrong default for a browsing history. If the user does want it, note that Hister refuses to start in public mode unless an access token or user handling is also configured, which is the one place upstream protects you."
  - "⛔⛔ THE REGISTRY IS NINE RELEASES BEHIND GITHUB, SO PIN THE DIGEST. Measured against ghcr.io on 2026-08-17: ghcr.io/asciimoo/hister carries 100 tags and the only version-shaped ones are v0.4.0, v0.5.0 and v0.5.0-root, while GitHub's newest release is v0.17.0. There is NO v0.17.0 image tag to pin. The rolling tag IS the current build: its index digest is sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:56c41949» and the amd64 image config inside it is labelled org.opencontainers.image.version v0.17.0, revision «REDACTED:longhex:d173c10e», created 2026-07-28, matching the release date. So reference the image BY DIGEST, which is reproducible, and re-derive the digest before a redeploy if you want the newer build. ⚠️ When you compare digests yourself, send an identical Accept header on every call, or you get a different manifest representation and therefore a different digest, which looks like a version change when nothing moved."
  - "⛔ SET server.base_url TO THE REAL PUBLIC HOSTNAME OR SEARCH BREAKS IN TWO SEPARATE WAYS, AND ONE OF THEM IS SILENT. Upstream's compose ships HISTER__SERVER__BASE_URL as http://localhost:4433. First: config.go:878-899 derives the WebSocket URL from base_url, so the browser UI will try to open ws://localhost:4433/search from the visitor's own machine and the search box simply never returns anything. Second: server.go:912-922, a search request that is not format=json and whose Origin is not the configured host is answered with a 500. So generate the dname yourself in the full hister-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form BEFORE deploying, and set HISTER__SERVER__BASE_URL to https://<that name>. A bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "⚠️ THE SEARCH BOX NEEDS WEBSOCKETS THROUGH redu's PROXY, AND THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO CHECK IF THE UI LOOKS DEAD. The browser opens wss://<host>/search and streams results over it; upstream's own nginx example exists purely to carry that upgrade, and their troubleshooting note is that if search does not work the problem is almost certainly the WebSocket. The plain HTTP path GET /search?q=...&format=json is NOT the same code path and will keep working even if the upgrade is broken, so DO NOT conclude from a working curl that the UI works. Test the UI in a browser, and if the box returns nothing while curl returns results, the upgrade is the cause."
  - "⛔ THE DATABASE SETTING IS A STRING-SNIFFING TRAP AND IT FAILS SILENTLY. config.go:784-786: server.database is treated as a PostgreSQL DSN if and only if the value CONTAINS AN EQUALS SIGN, and as an SQLite filename relative to app.directory otherwise. redu injects DATABASE_URL in postgres://user:[REDACTED:conn-password]@host:port/db form, which contains no equals sign, so pasting it in does not connect to Postgres at all, it asks SQLite to open a file whose name is that URL. If the user does want managed Postgres, build the key=value form instead: host=$PGHOST user=$PGUSER password=[REDACTED:value] dbname=$PGDATABASE port=$PGPORT sslmode=require."
  - "⛔ THIS RECIPE KEEPS SQLITE ON THE VOLUME ON PURPOSE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH READING BEFORE YOU CHANGE IT. Everywhere else in this library a managed Postgres is what makes a deployment durable. Here it does not, because the database is only one of three places Hister keeps state. The other two are on the filesystem in app.directory and cannot move: the bleve search index (server/indexer/indexer.go:377-383) and a content-addressed store under data/html and data/favicon holding the gzipped full HTML of every indexed page (server/indexer/datastore.go:17-21). The index can be rebuilt; THE STORED PAGE BODIES CANNOT, they are the only copy of what those pages looked like. So the volume is mandatory whatever you do with the database, and adding a managed Postgres at an extra GBP 0.0174/hr splits the state across two systems while leaving the irreplaceable half exactly where it was. Offer it as an option with that explanation, never as a silent upgrade."
  - "⛔ EVERYTHING IS ON THE VOLUME AT /hister/data, SO LOSE IT AND YOU LOSE THE INSTANCE. It holds the bleve index, data/html with the gzipped page bodies, data/favicon, .secret_key (config.go:260, which keys the session cookie store at server.go:172), rules.json, db.sqlite3 and config.yml. There is no encryption key to write down here, which makes this the closest equivalent: the volume IS the secret. The one value you must reuse on every redeploy is HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN, because it is configured into every client, the browser extension, the CLI and any MCP client; change it and all of them stop working at once with a 403."
  - "⚠️ DO NOT COPY user: '1000:1000' OUT OF THE DOCKER DOCS. IT IS WRONG AND IT WILL COST YOU AN HOUR. docker.md says the image runs as UID/GID 1000 and all three of its compose examples set that. The actual image config for the current build says 65532:65532, and Dockerfile:74 creates /hister/data inside the image owned by 65532. Set no user at all: docker seeds a new named volume with the ownership of the image directory it is mounted over, so 65532 gets a writable data directory for free, and forcing 1000 gives you a container that cannot write to its own volume."
  - "⛔ DELETE THE build: BLOCK AND THE HISTER_IMAGE INDIRECTION FROM UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE. Their compose.yml carries image: with a HISTER_IMAGE default AND a build: section targeting the release stage, which is right for a contributor and wrong on a VM with no source tree. Keep everything else from it, because the rest is genuinely good hardening you would otherwise have to write yourself: read_only true, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, init true and a 64 MB tmpfs on /tmp."
  - "PORT 4433, AND THE HEALTH PATH IS /. Dockerfile:82 exposes 4433 and its HEALTHCHECK simply wgets http://localhost:4433/. Pass 4433 to deploy_compose. There is no dedicated health endpoint, so for a scripted check use GET /api/config, which is anonymous by design and returns a JSON body you can assert on."
  - "THE DEPLOY IS NOT FINISHED WHEN THE CONTAINER IS HEALTHY, BECAUSE THE INSTANCE STARTS EMPTY. Hister indexes nothing by itself. Until the user installs the browser extension and authenticates it, or imports from Linkding, Linkwarden, Karakeep or Shaarli with the CLI, or points the crawler at something, every search correctly returns nothing. Say that when you hand over the URL, or a working deploy reads as a broken one. The extension authenticates by copying the session cookie from a logged-in web UI, so the user has to sign in with the access token in the same browser first."
  - "AN AGENT CAN SEARCH IT: POST /mcp IS AN MCP ENDPOINT. Authenticate it with Authorization: Bearer $HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN or the X-Access-Token header, the same value as app.access_token. Its tools include search, get_preview and get_history. That is the interesting half of this deploy for anyone using an agent: their own reading becomes a source the agent can query. It is also one more reason the token must be set: with app.public true this endpoint answers anonymously."
  - "DISK IS THE THING THAT GROWS, AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE FOR HOW FAST. A gzipped copy of the full HTML of every page visited accumulates on the volume forever; nothing in the docs states a rate or a ceiling and it depends entirely on how much the owner browses. m1.medium comes with 40 GB and growing it later is a volume resize rather than a redeploy. The two levers are app.disable_previews true, which stops storing page bodies at all and reclaims the existing ones on the next hister reindex, and indexer.max_file_size_mb, which defaults to 1. Measure du -sh on the data volume after a few weeks and write the number back into this file."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO MEMORY FIGURE ANYWHERE IN ITS DOCS. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) below is reasoning from what it is: a single static Go binary with an embedded bleve index, no interpreter and no JVM. # Self-host Hister on redu

A private search engine over the pages you actually read. Your browser sends each page to your own
Hister instance, which indexes the text and keeps a copy, and then you can search your own reading
the way you search the web. An MCP endpoint means your agent can search it too.

**About GBP 0.0278/hour, roughly GBP 20 a month**, one VM and no database. That fits the no-card
free trial.

## Read this before you deploy it

This is the most sensitive thing in this library. A Hister instance holds:

- every URL you visit, with its title and its extracted text,
- **a gzipped copy of the full HTML of every one of those pages**, kept by default so the preview
  pane works,
- your visit history.

Upstream put it best in their own server setup guide: *Hister transmits your entire browsing
history, with page contents, to and from the server.*

**And with the settings it ships with, there is no authentication at all.** That is not a
guess. In `server/server.go`, when neither `app.user_handling` nor `app.access_token` is
configured, every incoming request is given `Authenticated = true`, and no auth middleware is
attached to any route.

So this recipe sets `HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN` **at deploy time**, before the hostname ever
resolves. There is no window to close afterwards, and there is no signup form for anyone to reach
first. If you take one thing from this page: do not run Hister on a public hostname without that
variable set.

## What this deploys

- **Hister** from the official image, **pinned by digest** because the registry has no tag for
  this release (see below), on one m1.medium VM, port 4433.
- One volume on `/hister/data`, which holds the index, the stored page bodies, the SQLite
  database and the session signing key.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, with every content endpoint answering 403 to
  anyone without the token.

**No managed database, deliberately.** See the quirk: the irreplaceable half of Hister's state is
on the filesystem either way, so a Postgres VM would add cost without adding durability.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Hister on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

```bash

```

Put it in the project `.env` as `HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`, hand it to the user once in the
session, and never write it into this file.

## The three that actually break it

**The token.** Without `HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN` every anonymous request is treated as
authenticated. Nothing warns you, and the web UI looks completely normal.

**`base_url`.** Upstream's compose ships `http://localhost:4433`. Leave it and the browser
opens a WebSocket to the visitor's own machine, so the search box returns nothing forever, while
`curl` keeps working perfectly.

**The database string.** `server.database` is a Postgres DSN only if it contains an `=`.
Anything else, including a `postgres://` URL, is read as an SQLite filename.

## Prove the door is actually shut

The Memos lesson applies exactly here: a flag reporting the right value is not proof the behaviour
changed. This checks the flag, and then checks the behaviour the flag is supposed to guarantee,
in both directions.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Needs: HOST (the deployed hostname, no scheme) and HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN.
set -u

: "${HOST:?set HOST to the deployed hostname, without a scheme}"
: "${HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN:[REDACTED:value] HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN}"

INCONCLUSIVE=3
OUT=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$OUT"' EXIT

# The token goes in on stdin via a curl config, never in argv where ps can read it.
get() {                     # $1 = url, $2 = "auth" to send the token
  if [ "${2:-}" = "auth" ]; then
    printf 'header = "X-Access-Token: [REDACTED:value]"\nurl = "%s"\n' "$HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN" "$1" |
      curl -sS -K - -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}'
  else
    curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' "$1"
  fi
}

# 1. GATE. /api/config is anonymous by design and is how we prove we reached Hister at all.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/api/config")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the edge: the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"baseUrl"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/config answered $code without a Hister config body."
  head -c 200 "$OUT"; echo
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
echo "ok: talking to Hister"

# 2. The FLAG. Necessary, and on its own it proves nothing.
if ! grep -q '"authMode":"token"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "FAIL: authMode is not token, so HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN never reached the container"
  echo "and every request is being treated as authenticated. Do not leave this instance up."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: authMode reports token"

# 3a. POSITIVE HALF, and the one that makes the negative mean anything: the token opens search.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/search?q=redu&format=json" auth)
if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: search answered 404 even WITH the token, so the route has moved and the"
  echo "anonymous check below would pass vacuously. Do not leave this instance up."
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"search_duration"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: authenticated search answered $code without a results body."
  head -c 200 "$OUT"; echo
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
echo "ok: the token opens search"

# 3b. NEGATIVE HALF. Same URL, no token. withTokenAuth answers 403, not 401.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/search?q=redu&format=json")
if [ "$code" != "403" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous search answered $code, expected 403."
  echo "Anything else means a stranger can read this browsing history. Take it down."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: anonymous search is refused with 403"

# 4. The worst single thing to leak, checked separately.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/api/history")
if [ "$code" != "403" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous GET /api/history answered $code, expected 403."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: anonymous history is refused with 403"
echo "PASS"
```

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` a real failure that means taking the instance down, `3`
inconclusive. An empty index is fine here: an authenticated search on a brand new instance still
returns 200 with a results body, which is why this works before anything has been indexed.

## After it is up

Hister starts empty and indexes nothing on its own. To give it something to search:

1. Open the URL, sign in with the access token.
2. Install the browser extension and click **Authenticate Extension** in the same browser: it
   copies the session cookie from the logged-in web UI.
3. Or import from Linkding, Linkwarden, Karakeep or Shaarli with the CLI.

Then point your agent at `POST /mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer <your token>` and it can
search your own reading.

matching the release. So there is nothing to pin by version, and the digest is the pin:

    ghcr.io/asciimoo/hister@sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:56c41949»

That digest is the multi-architecture index, so it resolves correctly on amd64 and arm64.

## The compose

```yaml
services:
  hister:
    # Pinned by digest: the registry has no tag for this release. See the note above.
    image: ghcr.io/asciimoo/hister@sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:56c41949»
    init: true
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Upstream's own hardening, kept as it is. Do not add a user: line, the image is 65532.
    read_only: true
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    ports:
      - '4433:4433'
    volumes:
      - hister_data:/hister/data
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:noexec,nosuid,size=64m
    environment:
      HISTER__SERVER__ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:4433
      # THE FULL PUBLIC URL, generated before the deploy. Not a bare label, not localhost.
      HISTER__SERVER__BASE_URL: "https://hister-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud"
      # From the project .env. Without this, the whole instance is world-readable.
      HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN: "[REDACTED:value]}"

volumes:
  hister_data:
```

Generate the token alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in a header, a shell or JSON:

```bash
HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:08bdef6e» tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 40)
```

Put it in the project `.env` as `HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`, hand it to the user once in the
session, and never write it into this file.

## The three that actually break it

**The token.** Without `HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN` every anonymous request is treated as
authenticated. Nothing warns you, and the web UI looks completely normal.

**`base_url`.** Upstream's compose ships `http://localhost:4433`. Leave it and the browser
opens a WebSocket to the visitor's own machine, so the search box returns nothing forever, while
`curl` keeps working perfectly.

**The database string.** `server.database` is a Postgres DSN only if it contains an `=`.
Anything else, including a `postgres://` URL, is read as an SQLite filename.

## Prove the door is actually shut

The Memos lesson applies exactly here: a flag reporting the right value is not proof the behaviour
changed. This checks the flag, and then checks the behaviour the flag is supposed to guarantee,
in both directions.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Needs: HOST (the deployed hostname, no scheme) and HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN.
set -u

: "${HOST:?set HOST to the deployed hostname, without a scheme}"
: "${HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN:[REDACTED:value] HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN}"

INCONCLUSIVE=3
OUT=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$OUT"' EXIT

# The token goes in on stdin via a curl config, never in argv where ps can read it.
get() {                     # $1 = url, $2 = "auth" to send the token
  if [ "${2:-}" = "auth" ]; then
    printf 'header = "X-Access-Token: [REDACTED:value]"\nurl = "%s"\n' "$HISTER_ACCESS_TOKEN" "$1" |
      curl -sS -K - -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}'
  else
    curl -sS -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}' "$1"
  fi
}

# 1. GATE. /api/config is anonymous by design and is how we prove we reached Hister at all.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/api/config")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the edge: the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"baseUrl"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/config answered $code without a Hister config body."
  head -c 200 "$OUT"; echo
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
echo "ok: talking to Hister"

# 2. The FLAG. Necessary, and on its own it proves nothing.
if ! grep -q '"authMode":"token"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "FAIL: authMode is not token, so HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN never reached the container"
  echo "and every request is being treated as authenticated. Do not leave this instance up."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: authMode reports token"

# 3a. POSITIVE HALF, and the one that makes the negative mean anything: the token opens search.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/search?q=redu&format=json" auth)
if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: search answered 404 even WITH the token, so the route has moved and the"
  echo "anonymous check below would pass vacuously. Do not leave this instance up."
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"search_duration"' "$OUT"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: authenticated search answered $code without a results body."
  head -c 200 "$OUT"; echo
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
echo "ok: the token opens search"

# 3b. NEGATIVE HALF. Same URL, no token. withTokenAuth answers 403, not 401.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/search?q=redu&format=json")
if [ "$code" != "403" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous search answered $code, expected 403."
  echo "Anything else means a stranger can read this browsing history. Take it down."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: anonymous search is refused with 403"

# 4. The worst single thing to leak, checked separately.
code=$(get "https://$HOST/api/history")
if [ "$code" != "403" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous GET /api/history answered $code, expected 403."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: anonymous history is refused with 403"
echo "PASS"
```

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` a real failure that means taking the instance down, `3`
inconclusive. An empty index is fine here: an authenticated search on a brand new instance still
returns 200 with a results body, which is why this works before anything has been indexed.

## After it is up

Hister starts empty and indexes nothing on its own. To give it something to search:

1. Open the URL, sign in with the access token.
2. Install the browser extension and click **Authenticate Extension** in the same browser: it
   copies the session cookie from the logged-in web UI.
3. Or import from Linkding, Linkwarden, Karakeep or Shaarli with the CLI.

Then point your agent at `POST /mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer <your token>` and it can
search your own reading.

Everything is staged. Here's the plan — **nothing has been created yet, and nothing will be until you say go.**

## Read this part first — what this instance will hold

Hister is a personal search engine over the pages you *visit*. A browser extension pushes every page to it, and it keeps:

- every URL, with its title and extracted text,
- **a gzipped copy of the full HTML of every one of those pages** (default-on, for the preview pane),
- your visit history.

Including whatever was on screen behind a login. Upstream's own words: *Hister transmits your entire browsing history, with page contents, to and from the server.* This is the most sensitive thing in this library — worth a beat before approving.

With its shipped defaults **Hister has no authentication at all** (`server.go:296-302`: no `access_token` and no `user_handling` ⇒ every request gets `Authenticated = true`, and no auth middleware is attached to any route). So the deploy sets `HISTER__APP__ACCESS_TOKEN` **at creation time**, before the hostname ever resolves — there's no window to close afterwards and no signup form for a stranger to reach.

## What gets created

| | |
|---|---|
| **Image** | `ghcr.io/asciimoo/hister@sha256:2894138653…d7395` — pinned by digest; the registry's newest version tag is v0.5.0 while this build is v0.17.0, so there is nothing to pin by version |
| **VM** | 1 × m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB), flavor_id `3` |
| **Hostname** | `https://hister-fv24f1zp.redu.cloud` — generated up front and wired into `HISTER__SERVER__BASE_URL` |
| **Storage** | one volume at `/hister/data` — bleve index, gzipped page bodies, `.secret_key`, SQLite db |
| **Database** | none. SQLite on the same volume, deliberately |
| **Auth** | 40-char alphanumeric access token, passed into the project `.env` at deploy time |

**Cost: GBP 0.0278/hr — about GBP 20/month.** Fits the no-card free trial.

Two things I want to flag rather than bury:

- **plan_deploy quoted m1.large at GBP 35.48/mo.** It sizes multi-service compose stacks up because it can't tell a pulled image from a built one. I'm passing `flavor_id: "3"` explicitly to hold m1.medium at GBP 20.29/mo, which is what `redu.md` records and what a single static Go binary actually needs.
- **No managed Postgres, on purpose.** Elsewhere a managed DB is what makes a deploy durable; here it isn't. The irreplaceable state — the stored page bodies under `data/html` — lives on the filesystem either way and cannot move. Adding Postgres (+GBP 0.0174/hr) would split state across two systems while leaving the irreplaceable half exactly where it is. Available if you want it, but it buys nothing here.

One thing to expect: **the instance starts empty and indexes nothing by itself.** Until you install the browser extension and authenticate it, every search correctly returns nothing. A working deploy will look like a broken one for a bit.
